skill.name: convex-expert
skill.description: Convex backend specialist. Use this agent for any code inside a `convex/` directory — function definitions, schemas, indexes, queries, mutations, actions, HTTP endpoints, cron jobs, file storage, auth wiring, and component installation. Knows the object-form function syntax, validator patterns, resource limits, and component ecosystem that generic Claude routinely gets wrong.
skill.summary: Write and review Convex backend functions, validators, indexes, and schema changes.
skill.author: convex

security_audit.summary: One command finding is confirmed: the skill instructs the agent to run CLI commands and push backend changes. The other matches cover documentation, an environment file warning, or a Convex sign-in check. The push has no approval step, and no evidence of credential disclosure or audit manipulation was found.

remediation.issue: The verification workflow can push changes without explicit approval of the deployment target.
remediation.suggestion: Run a local type check first. Ask for approval before pushing or changing deployment bindings. Show the target and stop if sign-in or target verification fails.

remediation.issue: The verification instructions use npx without requiring a trusted local executable.
remediation.suggestion: Use the repository's locked TypeScript and Convex dependencies. Ask before fetching or installing any missing package.

content.value_statement: Convex changes can fail when validators, imports, or indexes do not match the project. This skill guides backend edits and reviews using Convex function, schema, and runtime conventions.
actual_capabilities: Inspect the project schema and generated guidance before editing Convex functions.
Draft object-form queries, mutations, and actions with argument and return validators.
Recommend indexes and bounded reads for tables that can grow.
Distinguish internal functions from client-facing functions.
Plan schema changes that backfill existing records before making fields required.
Explain when to separate Node actions from queries and mutations.
limitations: The skill focuses on Convex backend code, not frontend implementation.
The skill provides instructions, not a bundled compiler or deployment tool.
Type checking requires an available project toolchain and does not confirm deployment success.
The documented verification can push changes. Specify local-only verification unless you approve a specific deployment.

use_cases.title: Write a First Convex Query
use_cases.description: Add a typed query with argument and return validators that match the project schema.

use_cases.title: Bound a Growing Query
use_cases.description: Review a growing table and propose an index and pagination for its main read path.

use_cases.title: Plan a Schema Migration
use_cases.description: Plan how to introduce a field, backfill existing records, and then require the field.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Explain a Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the supplied Convex schema and query. Explain how the argument and return validators work. Do not edit files or run commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn how a registered function matches the schema.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Add Bounded Reads
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this Convex list query to use an index and pagination. Explain any schema changes. Do not push to a deployment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Replace an unbounded read on a growing table.

prompt_templates.title: Experienced: Separate Runtime Roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this module for mixed Node actions and database functions. Separate the runtimes and keep functions internal unless a client needs them. Do not deploy.
prompt_templates.scenario: Correct runtime placement and limit public exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Stage a Schema Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a migration for adding a required field to a populated table. Include an optional field, a backfill, and validation before tightening the schema. Do not run the migration.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a schema change for an existing deployment.

output_examples.input: Review a status-based list query on a growing orders table.
output_examples.output: Add an index on status and use it to paginate matching orders. Return one page at a time so the read remains bounded as the table grows.

output_examples.input: Plan a required owner field for a populated table.
output_examples.output: Introduce the field as optional and update new writes to populate it. Backfill older records and verify coverage before making the field required.

output_examples.input: Review a Node module that fetches data and writes database records.
output_examples.output: Keep the external request in a Node action. Put database writes in a separate internal mutation and call it from the action.

best_practices: Read the project schema and generated guidance before proposing backend changes.
Use argument and return validators and keep functions internal unless clients need direct access.
Check types locally and confirm the exact deployment target before approving any push.
anti_patterns: Collecting every record from a table that can grow.
Making a field required before existing records are backfilled.
Treating a successful Convex sign-in check as approval to deploy.

faq.question: Do I need an existing Convex project?
faq.answer: No for conceptual guidance. For project-specific edits, provide the repository or its schema and relevant functions.

faq.question: Does it help with query performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends indexes and bounded reads based on query access patterns.

faq.question: Can it review public and internal functions?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends internal functions by default and public functions when clients need direct access.

faq.question: Does it support Node actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains how to keep Node actions separate from queries and mutations.

faq.question: Can I request verification without deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. Specify local-only verification and disallow deployment or configuration changes.

faq.question: Does it support schema migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends adding optional fields, backfilling records, and checking coverage before applying stricter validation.
